verdict.rationale: mise ships its own event-triggered automation. First-party docs describe `mise watch` rebuilding automatically on file changes. Community users show `[hooks] postinstall` entries in mise.toml that run commands automatically after `mise install`. Coverage is narrow: the evidence shows only file-change watching and an install hook, not a general rule system for arbitrary events. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the hooks system and its supported events, a general event-to-action rule mechanism beyond file watching and postinstall, and detail on configuring watch triggers.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: mise watch to automatically rebuild on changes—no configuration required, but it helps
a [hooks] postinstall in mise.toml runs `uv sync` and `ansible-galaxy` role/collection installs
I always setup a postinstall hook so someone just runs `mise install` and gets correct tool versions plus dependencies installed.
